name: Tempest

F3.note: E3MHZ and E6MHZ gating to J19

R9.note: DIAG STEP, SELF TEST, SLAM, coin L/C/R, 3KHZ, HALT

notes: Symbols on these sheets: a square is the edge connector J20, a hexagon the interconnect J19, and an arrow a test point — so probe points are marked explicitly on the drawing.
Same MPU warning as Asteroids and Battlezone: the game clocks at 1.5 MHz so the part must be a 6502A. A plain 6502 tops out at 1 MHz and will not run.
Clock tree is near-identical to Battlezone: 12.096 MHz crystal into a 74193 for 6/3/1.5 MHz, and an LS393 for 3 kHz and 24 kHz.
A physical 'DIAG STEP' test pad is marked on the board next to the coin door input network — a probe point, not just a signal name.

The input architecture is identical to Battlezone: two 8-position DIP banks each read onto the data bus through its own LS244 under OPT0/OPT1, with a third LS244 for the coin door plus 3KHZ and HALT. Knowing one Atari board of this era gets you most of the way round another.
